papers.title: Ranked Right, Sized Wrong: Ensemble Spread Fails Silently at Streamflow Extremes
papers.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks, are increasingly used for operational streamflow forecasting, with ensemble spread providing a signal of predictive uncertainty. As climate change increases the frequency of hydroclimatic extremes, these models will increasingly operate under flow conditions that are rare in their historical records. We therefore evaluate whether ensemble spread remains informative under increasing flows, examining both its magnitude relative to error and its ability to rank errors. Prediction error is approximately $2\times$ the corrected spread at ordinary flows and up to $4\times$ at the highest flows, with the discrepancy increasing with flow (log-log slope $1.30$, 95% CI: $[1.20,1.41]$). Under-dispersion is strongest in observed extreme flows beyond the training record, reaching an $18\times$ discrepancy. This is pervasive and not explainable by conditional mean bias. Area Under the Sparsification Error, a standard distribution-free metric of uncertainty ranking, describing how well a model knows when it is uncertain, indicates near-oracle ranking for ensemble spread ($0.071$), yet ordering by predicted discharge alone nearly matches it. Informative uncertainty ranking can coexist with severe under-dispersion. In deployment, error ranking cannot be verified, yet the spread is available, and it is relied on as the uncertainty signal under increasingly extreme conditions, while systematically understating risk, most severely for the extreme events that matter most.

papers.title: Building and calibrating a 3Di subgrid flood model for Hanoi, without a surveyed terrain model, drainage data, or rain gauges
papers.abstract: Urban hydrodynamic flood models typically rely on a surveyed terrain model, an explicit pipe drainage network, and rain gauge measurements, none of which were available for the inundation following Typhoon Matmo in My Dinh and Tay Mo, Hanoi, on 7 October 2025. The present study addresses this issue by documenting the construction and calibration of a 32.8 km^2 3Di subgrid model under severe data constraints, demonstrating how unmonitored catchments can be simulated using openly accessible sources. Specifically, a 1 m digital elevation model was systematically repaired for river and lake bathymetry, unsurveyed water bodies, road underpasses, and an excavation pit to re-establish essential overland flow paths. In addition, assigned infiltration rates across land-cover classes were utilized to stand in for the unrecorded subsurface sewer system, while half-hourly satellite precipitation from the IMERG Late product provided rainfall forcing for a closed two-dimensional domain. Model calibration was conducted against eight crowdsourced depth observations. The simulation results demonstrated that six observation points retained surface water and were closely aligned with the reported values within 2.2 cm. However, two peripheral locations along Tay Mo Road and Road 70 remained completely dry in the model. Because all eight points were utilized during parameter adjustment and no independent validation dataset was withheld, this correspondence reflects a calibration fit rather than an unconstrained predictive test.

papers.title: The Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP): Towards standardisation of global glacier projections
papers.abstract: The Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP) provides an international framework for the coordinated evaluation and comparison of global glacier evolution models and their projections of glacier change. Its fourth phase, GlacierMIP4, updates previous global glacier projections through a standardised experimental design. For the first time, the protocol includes simulations extending to 2300 and an overshoot scenario for a subset of climate projections and requires monthly output of individual mass-balance components such as melt, accumulation and refreezing, in addition to annual results for glacier mass and area. While permitting model-specific approaches to calibration and other aspects of model implementation, the protocol prescribes common atmospheric forcing data, inventory boundary conditions, and reporting conventions to enable consistent analyses of inter-model differences. Here, we describe the GlacierMIP4 experimental protocol, including the simulation domain, initialisation, atmospheric forcing, and standardised output requirements. More broadly, we emphasize the need for standardised terminology, units, sign convention and file formats in global glacier modelling to improve the traceability, interoperability, and comparability of results, and recommend this protocol as a blueprint for future global glacier modelling studies.

papers.title: Learning relaxation time distributions from spectral induced polarization data with a complex-valued variational autoencoder
papers.abstract: Spectral induced polarization (SIP) is a geophysical method used to characterize subsurface materials. It measures the frequency-dependent complex electrical resistivity of rocks and soils through the application of an alternating current. Debye and Warburg decompositions are standard methods for analyzing and interpreting SIP data, as they allow estimation of the relaxation time distribution (RTD) of geomaterials. However, conventional decomposition approaches treat measurements independently, work in real-valued spaces despite the complex-valued nature of SIP data, and provide limited uncertainty quantification. These limitations reduce the effectiveness of conventional decomposition on heterogeneous datasets. We reformulate the decomposition approach as an unsupervised machine learning problem and introduce a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) that learns a shared mapping from SIP datasets to continuous RTDs. The model is validated on a dataset comprising 140 laboratory and field SIP measurements of granular mixtures, sedimentary and igneous rock, and cementitious materials. The CVAE operates in complex-valued data space and achieves reconstruction errors of 0.53 % and 0.27 % for the imaginary and phase components of resistivity, respectively, with evidence of improvement over conventional methods at corresponding p-values of 0.007 and 0.06. The inferred RTDs are stable and physically consistent, and their total chargeability and mean relaxation time correlate with polarizable grain content and grain size, respectively, with coefficients of determination up to 0.98. An additional contribution of the proposed method is the learned latent representation, which organizes SIP spectra into a structured space. Unsupervised clustering in a two-dimensional projection of this space improves the silhouette score by nearly a factor of two relative to conventional RTD parameters.
